concepts.def: Switching between varieties or languages mid-talk
Adjusting your speech to match listeners
Moving your speech CLOSER to others
Moving your speech AWAY from others
Status gained by using non-standard forms
Status from using the 'standard' high-status form

walkthroughs.body_html: You don't talk to your gran the way you talk to your mates — that's codeswitching.

Howard Giles: we converge with people we want to bond with, and diverge to keep distance.

Job interview? You converge towards their formality.

Overt: 'posh' RP gets you respect from teachers.

Covert: dropping 'Hs' and using slang earns respect within your friend group.

Both are prestige — just different audiences.

mcqs.q: A teenager speaking Standard English in class but slang with friends is doing what?
options: Accommodating only
Codeswitching
Diverging only
Using idiolect
Speaking like Shakespeare
Moving your speech towards your listener's
Moving your speech away from your listener's
Refusing to change your speech
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.
Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between semantics and pragmatics?
options: Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
Semantics is grammar and pragmatics is vocabulary.
Semantics studies literal meaning of words and sentences; pragmatics studies how meaning depends on context, speaker intention and conversational implicature.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.
